title: A bridge, a boat, a lamp
hookLine: the friend who always does the airport run; Shantideva wishes to be a bridge, a boat, a lamp
carry: the bodhisattva's wish: to be the way across
tomorrow: how does a blind man find a jewel in the trash?

cards: Every friend group has one. The person who does the airport run at five in the morning. Who explains the bus system to the new kid.
Who leaves the porch light on when someone's coming home late. They rarely get thanked. They don't end up in the photos, because they're the ones holding the phone.
They're just how everyone else gets where they're going. So, what else does Shantideva wish to be? Things exactly like that.

teach.h: A GUIDE, A BOAT, A BRIDGE.
teach.b: A few verses after the medicine, Shantideva's list grows. May I be a protector for those who have none, and a guide for travelers. For those who want to cross the water, may I be a boat, a bridge, a causeway.
A lamp for anyone who needs light. A bed for anyone who needs rest. A servant for all who need one.
Look at what's on that list. Not one of them is the destination. A bridge doesn't come along to the other side and ask for a seat at dinner.
A boat drops you at the shore and goes back for the next person.

teach.h: A LAMP, A BED, A SERVANT.
teach.b: A lamp lights the page; nobody reads the lamp.

Every item is something used, and then left behind, without a thank-you. That's the point. The awakening mind he's been building since chapter one wants to be the way across for other people, not the place they arrive.
And notice the size of it. You don't have to be a boat for everyone today.

teach.h: ONE CROSSING IS STILL A CROSSING.
teach.b: One crossing is still a crossing. One lamp is enough for one page.

teach.h: A BRIDGE, A BOAT, A LAMP.
teach.b: A bridge, a boat, a lamp.

how: Some Mahayana Buddhists recite this run of verses, may I be a protector, a guide, a boat, a bridge, a lamp, as part of daily practice, and some teachers ask students to choose one image to live by for a day.

o: being the way across for someone, then left behind
a temple built where two rivers meet each other
the journey a monk takes to reach a far monastery

p: for those who want to cross the water

s: Shantideva wishes to be the place people finally arrive
every item on his list is a way across, used and left behind, never the destination.
his list includes a boat, a bridge and a causeway
for those who want to cross the water, plus a guide, a lamp, a bed and a servant.
to live this verse you have to help everyone at once
one crossing is still a crossing. one lamp is enough for one page.

games.q: a new coworker is lost in the company's systems and too shy to ask. you're busy. what fits Shantideva's list?
o: wait for her to ask; offering help might seem pushy.
show her the one thing she's stuck on, and where to find the rest.
take over her project for the week so she doesn't have to struggle.
games.why: a bridge gets someone across and stays behind. you don't carry her the whole way; you help her cross one gap.

practice: Think of one person who's stuck on some small crossing: a question, a lonely week, a hard first day. Write them a short text that helps them across, a tip, a link, a ride offered, or just a light left on.
Read it once slowly, and send it now or when the sit ends.

wordCard.voice: A bridge: one of Shantideva's wishes, to be the way across for anyone who needs to cross, and then be left behind.

orig.note: Sanskrit: bridge, causeway. One of the things Shantideva wishes to be for those who want to cross.

carryVoice: Your line: the bodhisattva's wish, to be the way across. A bridge, a boat, a lamp: nobody reads the lamp, and the page still gets read. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bodhicaryavatara 3.17-3.18 (a protector, a guide, a boat, a bridge, a causeway; a lamp, a bed, a servant)
